title: PLAS-20K protein-ligand MD ensemble for PDB 3m0i bound to ZST: 5 replica trajectories of 40 frames, protein and ligand only, with the original investigators' AMBER topology.
description:
Metadata imported from https://mdrepo.org/explore/MDR00079393.

All-atom molecular dynamics of the protein-ligand complex 3m0i bound to CCD component ZST, drawn from the PLAS-20K dataset. This submission bundles 5 independent replica trajectories that share one topology. Each replica covers 0-3900 ps of production sampling at 100 ps between frames (40 frames). System: 5187 atoms across 318 residues, of which 41 belong to the ligand. The ligand net charge is +0, summed from the partial charges in the authors' own topology -- i.e. the charge the trajectory was generated with, not one inferred from a reference entry. The system also contains 1 cofactor (NAP), carrying the authors' parameters in the same way. Solvent has been stripped: the deposited trajectories contain protein, ligand and any cofactors only. The underlying simulation was run fully solvated in TIP3P. The source replica files carry the solute plus the two crystal waters the authors selected as the closest to both protein and ligand; those two waters are stripped here, and the source files contain no counter-ions to strip. Trajectories are deposited in mdcompress (.mdc) format at a coordinate resolution of 1000 fm (0.01 Angstrom). This compression is lossy in the same sense that the .xtc format is: positions are quantised, and the quantum is far below both the thermal fluctuation of the underlying sampling and the precision of the source coordinates. Every replica was decompressed and compared frame by frame against the uncompressed original before submission; the deviation is reported per complex in the QC record. The AMBER topology accompanying this submission is the ORIGINAL INVESTIGATORS' OWN BUILD, not a reconstruction. The published dataset ships coordinates only, but the authors separately released their topologies, and this is theirs: the protein+ligand system of their own tleap build (leaprc.protein.ff14SB + leaprc.gaff2, ligand and cofactor parameters from antechamber GAFF2/AM1-BCC), with the two crystal waters they carried in their solute unit removed to match the deposited trajectories. Nothing in it was recomputed here. Consequently the parameters are the ones the trajectory was actually generated with, rather than an equivalent rebuilt under a later AmberTools whose GAFF2 differs by up to 0.55 e on ligand charges. The correspondence was not assumed: every complex passed an automated QC gate (atom/residue/element sequence identity against the trajectory, bond-length sanity on each replica, and coordinate round-trip fidelity through both the NetCDF conversion and the mdc compression), and complexes whose released topology disagreed with their own trajectory were rejected rather than repaired. Source data: PLAS-20K (Korlepara et al., Scientific Data 11, 180 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02872-y), produced by IIIT Hyderabad (devalab) and distributed by IIIT-H / iHub-Data. Upstream copy used: version2 (india-data.org PLAS-20K-Variation2 mirror).
